claims.text: Random distributions of multiple principal elements in refractory high-entropy alloys induce severe local lattice distortions.
Local lattice distortions shift edge-dislocation cores away from their neutral slip planes and produce wavy, non-planar dislocation lines.
Wavy dislocation lines limit dislocation mobility.
Lattice-distortion-induced wavy dislocations cause refractory HEAs to retain relatively high yield strength as temperature increases.
Refractory HEAs exhibit only moderate changes in elastic anisotropy with increasing temperature compared with conventional BCC metals.
Homogenized NbTaTiV can remain a single-phase BCC alloy up to 900 °C.
The cited NbTaTiV alloy was produced by arc melting followed by high-temperature homogenization.
The homogenized NbTaTiV alloy has a grain-size range of approximately 200–400 μm.
The initial NbTaTiV alloy exhibits significant lattice distortion.
Atomic-size and modulus mismatches among constituent elements impose local lattice strains.
At room temperature, NbTaTiV displays nearly isotropic elastic behavior with a Zener anisotropy ratio of about 1.2.
Wavy edge-dislocation configurations are responsible for the low elastic anisotropy at lower temperatures.
At high temperatures, impeded dislocation motion moderates the rate of strength loss relative to conventional BCC alloys.
Elastic anisotropy in NbTaTiV increases gradually at elevated temperatures.
Conventional BCC alloys have less-impeded dislocation motion than the refractory HEA.
The HEA will show a smaller temperature-induced reduction in yield strength than a conventional BCC reference.
The HEA's Zener anisotropy ratio will rise from approximately 1.2 at room temperature to approximately 1.6 at 900 °C.
Wavy dislocation lines will be pronounced in the HEA but absent or much less pronounced in the conventional BCC reference.
The cited NbTaTiV system was compression-tested at room temperature, 500 °C, 700 °C, and 900 °C at a strain rate of 1 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹.
Preventing oxidation is necessary because oxidation could alter dislocation behavior.

contradictions.description: The main comparison fixes the strain rate at 1 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹, whereas the falsification experiment proposes measuring dislocation mobility through strain-rate sensitivity, which ordinarily requires tests at multiple strain rates.
